### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 46 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f9e5f31f72d66428a5e0595198b37b6b5d059938` — the merge of head `68effe33f34bb0004a595f724088b546b08e8827` into base `45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f9e5f31f72d66428a5e0595198b37b6b5d059938 && git checkout f9e5f31f72d66428a5e0595198b37b6b5d059938
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359 68effe33f34bb0004a595f724088b546b08e8827 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359 && git merge --no-ff 68effe33f34bb0004a595f724088b546b08e8827

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45efba2a5b0ccb12b16160b5b177b46416dbf359` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8437d513daacc57ca45e654c27563516b69f47d0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/packageless-overlays.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx, .changeset/28576-packageless-overlay-write-closed.md

Inputs read: card #28576 body and its four comments (the #28644 ruling-4 reading, the #28413 pointer, the triage unblock, the seat's claim); PR #28850 body, file list (30 paths) and the net diff against `main`; the 64 check-runs on the head: 56 `success`, 8 `skipped` (UI Published Artifacts, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate ×3 shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Schedule gate, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness). None pending, none failed. The dogfood battery is therefore NOT measured by CI on this head; the body's 376/4 run is the dev's own account.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Narrowed, right.** `saveMetaItem` (authoring saves: `source` unset, not `package-duplicate`), `publishMetaItem`, `deleteMetaItem` (`state !== 'draft'`) and `rollbackMetaItem` (on `rollbackPackageId`) now refuse `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` a write naming no package onto a `view`, `dashboard`, `report`, `translation` or `email_template` that a read-only code package ships (`packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal`, registry reads only, ahead of the override write gate and the lock gate). This is ADR-0146 D11 "Close" and the card's Wanted 1–2, including D1's rollback and reset. Right.
- **Carve-outs, right as far as they go.** A write naming any package; a name no read-only package ships (environment metadata, D11 "is not touched"); a draft discard (`state: 'draft'`); a name whose shippers all have ids `customizationPackageId` refuses (`no_pair`). The first three follow D11. The fourth is the dev's own reading ("D11 closes only what it has migrated") — sound in itself, but see ④ M1: it is applied to `no_pair` alone and not to the other dispositions the ceremony leaves.
- **One reading of "packaged" for close and ceremony, right.** `readOnlyShippingPackages` is now the shared predicate of `listPackagelessOverlays` and `overlayBaseShippers`; neither widens or narrows the census population. Not re-exported from `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`; `PackagedBaseRefusalHost` and `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal` are not either — no public TS surface moves.
- **Widened, right and declared.** Ruling 4 (#28644 item 1, card comment `6557820698`): a rollback of the pair's own declared row is stored `runtime-only` and judged by `overrideWriteVerdict` into the pair, where before `isArtifactBacked` alone made it `override-artifact`. A rollback the store previously sealed is now admitted — this is the widening that earns `Clause-②: yes`.
- **Removed, right.** #28413 item 4's allowance (`packagelessPairLanding`, `isPackagelessAuthoringSave`, the late `overrides`-keeping graft) and its pins; the card retires it with the write.
- **Console, right.** `StudioReadOnlyLink` no longer links an `allowEnvironmentOverlay` item to Setup (D11 "Retire", #27927 link). Setup shows the server's 403 verbatim; it sends `readActivePackageBinding()` as `packageId` when the page holds a `?package=`, and nothing otherwise — so a Setup page opened on the pair keeps its save.
- **Not changed, right.** `packagelessAddress` keeps its body (reads of unmigrated rows use it; every write door refuses before it resolves); the read envelope's `editable`/`deletable` and `packagedBaseRefusal` keep their answers.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/28576-packageless-overlay-write-closed.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/skills: patch`, `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; **BREAKING** banner; one marker `adr-0087: registered packageless-overlay-write-closed`, whose id this diff adds under `entries/semantic/` (the registry is generated from the template at build, so no committed index is owed). FROM → TO carried with the one-line fix and the pre-upgrade ceremony order the card's Wanted 4 asked for.

- `yes (narrowing)`: right — the diff narrows the four doors and widens the pair-row rollback (①). The AGENTS.md grammar allows `yes` plus the `(narrowing)` arm; the gate's own fixture names that very case.
- `narrowed` + `minor` on metadata-protocol: right — a requirement tightened on what a metadata author writes, and `minor` with BREAKING is the launch-window rule `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces; the card's "major" is superseded by that gate, which the body records as the deviation.
- `spec: patch`: right — the spec change is an additive registration (one semantic entry), not a narrowing of anything a spec author writes; per-package mixed levels have precedent (`.changeset/26725-object-duplicate-action-name.md`).
- `skills: patch`, `app-shell: patch`: right (prose; a link removed).
- PR body carries the same two declaration lines, line-initial. Check Changeset and ADR-0087 registration both `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`minor`, not `major`** — answered by the gate and the changeset's BREAKING banner; the card's Wanted 4 is met in the launch-window form. Closed.
2. **Fallout beyond the order's two re-judged files** (five more test files, the runtime reload test) — tests in the lane's remainder; CI green. Closed.
3. **Skills line trimmed to fit the token ceiling** — judged in ④ S3: the trim removed the object of "wins", and the sentence now under-teaches. Should-fix.
4. **Dead i18n key `engine.studio.pkg.readonlyLink`** left in `@object-ui/i18n`, report-only lister names it — lane's remainder; no card named. Noted, not blocking.
5. **Open question: a sending locale the base does not ship** (`zh-CN` row of `showcase_task_done_email`) — the dev measured that the ceremony `failed` to move it, the doors now refuse its package-less save and reset, and "its refusal still says the ceremony moves it". This is one member of the stranded-row class in ④ M1, not a separate question: the body "leaves it for" #28779's ruling but files nothing and the entry under review says nothing about it. Escalated into M1; the record requires the entry to name the row class and the dev to put the question on #28779 or a card, by number.
6. **Out of scope, noted: `?package=BASE` save of an overlay type lands an overlay bound to the read-only base** — the dev reads it against D1 and leaves it. A write onto a read-only package's own partition that D1 says is offered only on the writable package, with no card. Should-fix: file it; it is not this card's write and does not block here.
7. **Dogfood battery: 4 clock-dependent reds on the 18.0 upgrade fixtures**, "reasoned from the code and the two runs, not run on `main`" — and the Dogfood Regression Gate is `skipped` on this head, so nothing in CI measures the 26 re-routed dogfood cases either. Stated as unmeasured, not green; not a hits finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts`** — judged against ADR-0146 D11 and D1, the ceremony `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/packageless-overlays.ts` and its census `listPackagelessOverlays`, the doors in `protocol.ts` and `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal`, and the `SemanticMigration` contract (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; prose surfaces are the sibling convention, e.g. `18.security-catalog-environment-overlay-refused.ts`). Shape: well-formed, kebab id, right major prefix, fields filled; the id matches the changeset marker; `replacement` names `os migrate packageless-overlays` and `--apply`, both of which exist at this head with those spellings; the FROM → TO it describes is the one the save door enforces.

- **M1 — must-fix. The entry's prescription does not clear every row the close strands, and its acceptance test passes while such rows remain.** Read in the tree: the refusal is registry-only — any read-only shipper whose id derives a pair closes the write, whatever the stored row holds. The census classifies the same rows into `movable`, `multi_shipped`, `no_pair`, `foreign_declaration`, `shadowed`; `--apply` moves `movable` only, and a `movable` row can still end `failed` (the body's unshipped-locale case). Of the rows the ceremony leaves, the code keeps a door open for `no_pair` alone. For a `multi_shipped` row (two read-only packages ship the name — at least one pair derives, so the write is closed), a `foreign_declaration` row (one shipper with a pair — closed) and a `failed` row, after the upgrade: the package-less save, publish, delete and rollback answer 403; the ceremony lists and does not move them; and the ceremony's own printed remedies — `multi_shipped`: "move it by hand into the pair … or delete it"; `foreign_declaration`: "correct or remove the key, then re-run" — are exactly the package-less delete and save this PR closes. The `multi_shipped` row is still SERVED: `packagelessContentPackage` answers `null` (the unbound row alone) when several ship the name and no stored row is bound to one, and D8 item 1 keeps the unbound row over the code package. So a deployment that follows the entry to the letter can carry a served customization with no door, and the refusal it reads says the ceremony "moves it" (sole-shipper wording) or "lists it for you to place" — placing writes the pair, but the stale unbound row still wins the package-less read and cannot be removed. The entry says of these rows only that "a name several packages ship, or one whose package id forms no pair, is listed by the command and left for the operator" — it omits `foreign_declaration`, `shadowed` (which does have a door: "Restore package original", then re-run) and `failed`, and names nothing the operator can do after the upgrade. Its `acceptanceCriteria` — "reports nothing movable (exit 0)" — is satisfied with every such row present, and "(exit 0)" is no evidence at all: the preview exits 0 whenever it ran, movable rows or not (`exitCode` is 1 only under `--apply` with a `failed` outcome). Fix owed in the entry: say that every row the preview LISTS, not only the movable ones, is to be resolved on the release before this one — moved by `--apply`, re-placed into the right pair and the unbound row deleted, or its `overrides` key corrected — because after the upgrade those rows have no write door; name the five dispositions; make the criterion "the preview lists no row" and drop the exit-code clause. If instead the lane widens the code's carve-out to every disposition the ceremony leaves (as `no_pair` already is), or gives the ceremony a delete for listed rows, the entry must then say which; either way the stale `multi_shipped` and `shadowed` "delete this package-less row" lines in the ceremony's `reasonOf` are wrong at this head and are the lane's to fix with it. Rule-level only; nothing here is security-relevant.
- **S1 — should-fix.** `surface` says Setup's form save and reset "send none". `ResourceEditPage.tsx` sends `packageId: readActivePackageBinding()` on save, publish, reset and draft discard whenever the page holds a `?package=` (the card's own measurement at `:535`/`:2142`); only a page with no binding sends none. Say "when the page holds no `?package=`".
- **S2 — should-fix.** The ceremony composes the stack as `os serve` does and takes `--preset` and `--dev` ("pass it when the deployment boots with --dev"). A census run without the deployment's composition reads a different set of shipping packages and classifies rows differently (a name shipped only by a dev-composed plugin reads as environment metadata). The sibling entry `18.security-catalog-environment-overlay-refused.ts` names the flags; this one should.

**`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`** (the ADR-0146 paragraph, one hunk) — judged against the paragraph it replaces on `main`, the read order in `servedOverlayRowCandidates` (pair's declared override → the package's own row → the unbound row, for a read that serves the package's name), the census's `shadowed` disposition, and the doors above. The types it names for the honoured read (view, dashboard, report, email_template, translation, flow) are the five the close covers plus `flow`, which `refusePackagedBaseOverride` seals already — no type is named that the code leaves open, and none the code closes is unnamed. "D11 refuses new ones" is true of the code. The export sentence's dropped clause ("the base's is unchanged") is implied by "replaces the base's document whole"; no loss.

- **S3 — should-fix.** The sentence "a pre-D11 package-unbound Setup row wins until migrated" lost its object. On `main` it read "wins over the base's", which is what the code does (D8 item 1); the pair's declared override is served AHEAD of the unbound row (`servedOverlayRowCandidates`; the ceremony calls such a row `shadowed` and says the pair's row is the one served). Read as written, the shorter sentence teaches that a pre-D11 row beats the pair's override, which is false. Restore "over the base's", and — since this paragraph is the skill's only teaching of the rule and the #28413 pointer makes the refusal the place the ceremony is named — name `os migrate packageless-overlays` and say the pre-D11 row's package-less save, reset and rollback are refused too, not only "new ones". A few tokens; the ceiling gate will say if they fit.

No must-fix on the skill file. One must-fix on the migration entry (M1) — a FAIL.
